In this subsection, we are interested in positive bounded stationary states of (1) . By
positive, we mean positive componentwise in $\mathbb{R}^n$ since, from the strong elliptic maximum
principle applied to this cooperative system, if a bounded stationary state is nonnegative
componentwise in $\mathbb{R}^n$ , it is either positive componentwise, or identically $0$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$ . From
the confining properties of the fitnesses $r_i$ , any positive bounded stationary state of (1)
necessarily decays to $0$ exponentially as $\|\mathbf{x}\| \to +\infty$ . Therefore, it follows from Theorem 2.1
and the proof of Proposition 2.2 that (1) has no positive bounded stationary state if $\lambda_H \geq 0$
(see Remark 6.2 below for further details).

From the confining properties of the fitnesses $r_i$ , any positive bounded stationary state of (1) necessarily decays to $0$ exponentially as $\|\mathbf{x}\| \to +\infty$ .
